description: Meet the invisible rulers of the Earth, from ancient extremophiles to viruses and fungi.

slides.title: Welcome to Microbial Diversity
slides.content:
# Microbial Diversity

Welcome to Microbiology! This is the study of organisms too small to be seen with the naked eye. Despite their size, they run the planet.

## What You Will Learn:
- **Microbial Diversity** - The hidden world of the very small
- **Virus Structure** - The edge of life
- **Fungi Characteristics** - Yeasts, molds, and mushrooms
- **Protozoa Life Cycles** - Complex single-celled hunters

> **Fun Fact:** There are more bacterial cells in and on your body than there are human cells. You are more microbe than human!

slides.title: The Microbial World
slides.content:
# Domains of Life

Microbes are found in all three domains of life.

## 1. Bacteria (Prokaryotes):
- Single-celled, no nucleus. Peptidoglycan cell walls. Ubiquitous in every environment.

## 2. Archaea (Prokaryotes):
- Single-celled, no nucleus. Unique cell walls (no peptidoglycan). 
- Famous for being **extremophiles**: living in boiling hot springs, hypersaline lakes, or deep-sea hydrothermal vents.

## 3. Eukarya (Eukaryotes):
- Have a true nucleus. Includes Fungi, Protozoa, and Algae.

*(Note: Viruses are not considered living and don't fit into these domains!)*

slides.title: Viruses
slides.content:
# Viruses: The Ultimate Parasites

Are they alive? Most biologists say no, because they cannot reproduce or metabolize on their own.

## Structure:
- Extremely simple and incredibly small (much smaller than bacteria).
- **Nucleic Acid Core:** Contains the genetic code. Can be DNA or RNA, single-stranded or double-stranded.
- **Capsid:** A protective protein coat surrounding the genetic material.
- **Envelope (Optional):** Some viruses (like HIV or Influenza) steal a lipid membrane from the host cell as they exit, wrapping themselves in it to help infect the next cell.

## The Mechanism:
A virus must hijack a living host cell. It injects its genetic code, forcing the host's ribosomes and enzymes to build thousands of new viruses, eventually bursting (lysing) and killing the host cell.

slides.title: Fungi
slides.content:
# Kingdom Fungi

Fungi are eukaryotic, heterotrophic (cannot make their own food) organisms.

## Key Characteristics:
- **Cell Wall:** Made of **chitin** (the same tough material found in insect exoskeletons), NOT cellulose like plants.
- **Body Structure:** Most are multicellular and consist of a vast network of fine, thread-like filaments called **hyphae**. The entire mass of hyphae is called the mycelium. (Yeast is an exception; it is unicellular).
- **Nutrition:** They are absorptive heterotrophs. They secrete digestive enzymes OUTSIDE their body into the environment, break down organic matter, and then absorb the nutrients. 
- Excellent decomposers (saprophytes).

slides.title: Protozoa
slides.content:
# Protozoa: The First Animals

Protozoa are single-celled Eukaryotes that behave remarkably like tiny animals.

## Key Characteristics:
- They lack a rigid cell wall (unlike algae or fungi).
- Most are highly motile (they can move around).
- They are heterotrophic, often actively hunting and engulfing smaller microbes (like bacteria) via phagocytosis.

## Classification by Movement:
1. **Amoeboids:** Move using pseudopodia ('false feet' - cytoplasmic extensions). E.g., Amoeba.
2. **Flagellates:** Move using one or more long whip-like flagella. E.g., Trypanosoma (causes sleeping sickness).
3. **Ciliates:** Move using thousands of tiny, beating hair-like cilia. E.g., Paramecium.
4. **Sporozoans:** Non-motile. All are internal parasites with complex life cycles. E.g., Plasmodium (causes Malaria).

slides.title: Summary: Microbial Diversity
slides.content:
# Summary

## Key Concepts Reviewed:

- **Domains:** Microbes span Bacteria, Archaea (extremophiles), and Eukarya (Fungi/Protozoa).
- **Viruses:** Non-living obligate parasites. Consist simply of genetic material (DNA or RNA) wrapped in a protein capsid.
- **Fungi:** Eukaryotes with chitin cell walls. Form networks of hyphae (mycelium). Secrete enzymes to digest food externally.
- **Protozoa:** Animal-like, single-celled eukaryotes without cell walls. Classified by movement: pseudopodia, flagella, cilia, or non-motile parasites (sporozoans).

> **Congratulations!** You have completed the Microbial Diversity module.
